top_choice_rationale: Targeted protein degradation by bifunctional E3-recruiting molecules passes the game-changer test: a chemically simple idea, independently reproduced, that does something an inhibitor cannot. Crews and Deshaies (2001) and Ciulli (VHL ligands, ternary-complex structure) give a clean three-name attribution to one definable achievement, with the citation kept off the cereblon molecular-glue mechanism. The shared reservation is that no degrader is approved yet, but base editing carries the same maturity gap, so it cannot separate them; I rank base editing second because its Kondo and Nishida attribution is less clean. Nitrogenase structure is solid but leaves the mechanism open, and phase separation is still contested in vivo, so both rank below an award for either leading proposal, and an award still ranks above no award.
